images.name: 05-seed-keeping
images.prompt: Editorial watercolor and gouache illustration on ivory paper, wide 3:2 composition, for an article about seed exchange in Niyamgiri. Show two adult Dongria women seated facing one another, quietly transferring a small folded packet of seeds between their hands. Mid-distance view includes faces, hands and clothing, soft wooded hill background. CLOTHING REFERENCE attached: use only the two women in off-white wrapped garments at centre and right of the market photograph: simple white cotton drapes with narrow pink-red borders, a few bead necklaces, hair pins and restrained ear/nose ornaments. Do not use the tourist's clothing on the left. Do not copy any real person's identity. Different natural poses and ages, practical clothing, no performance necklaces, no elaborate ceremonial regalia. Seeds are small abstract grains, not an identified cultivar. Hands visibly support the packet with plausible grip. No decorative crop diagrams, text, invented symbols, ritual props or exact village reconstruction. An imagined respectful scene, painterly and selective, not a documentary photograph.
images.reference: Pillai Sree Vidya, Dangaria women 02, CC BY-SA 4.0; two women at centre/right used as clothing reference
images.limits: Interpretive imagined scene; not named people, a documented event, or community-reviewed evidence.

images.name: 06-forest-foods
images.prompt: Wide 3:2 editorial watercolor and gouache on warm ivory paper for an article about forest foods and home gardens in Rayagada. Imagined Dongria-inspired small home garden at the edge of wooded Niyamgiri hills. One adult woman seen three-quarter side view crouches beside a leafy vegetable bed, checking a leaf gently; a small plain woven gathering basket rests beside her. A few irregular garden patches, no picturesque abundance. Use attached market photo ONLY as clothing reference for the two women at centre/right: off-white cotton drape with narrow red-pink border, short dark hair held with metal pins, modest bead strand, restrained small ear/nose ornaments. Do not copy real faces or use tourist at left as reference. Fabric drapes naturally and hands contact the plant believably. No performance regalia, generic tribal symbols, murals, mushroom identification, words, captions or invented ritual. Distinct unposed solitary scene, grounded materials and selective painterly detail, everyday gardening rather than costume display. Not a documented household or identifiable plant guide.

images.name: 08-homes-and-repair
images.prompt: Make a wide 3:2 editorial watercolor/gouache illustration on warm ivory paper for 'Homes and the work of repair in Niyamgiri'. Subject is a modest earthen Dongria house form grounded in the July2016 Kalpavriksh study: adobe/earthen walls, wooden posts, steeply pitched grass-thatch roof reaching low at the eaves; another similar home partly visible along a parallel row on a gentle hill slope. Close oblique architectural view, dwelling and the roof materials foregrounded, green hills receding. Show a few bundles of dry thatching grass lying beside a wooden post, preparing for maintenance. NO people are needed, no palace, no ornate shrine, no generic tribal wall paintings or invented symbolic motifs, no modern toolbox or corrugated metal, no text. Not a specific named village or a claim all current Dongria homes are like this; the scene is interpretive architecture inspired by a dated description. Naturally uneven earthen surfaces but not theatrical poverty or picturesque damage. Roof slopes and timber support physically plausible, selective detailed grasses, quiet restrained palette. No dramatic sunset, HDR or photorealism.
images.reference: Kalpavriksh July 2016 Niyamgiri study printed p6
images.limits: Interpretive imagined scene; not named people, a documented event, or community-reviewed evidence.

images.name: 09-learning-and-belonging
images.prompt: Wide 3:2 editorial watercolor/gouache illustration on warm paper for learning and belonging in Niyamgiri. Three-quarter view of an imagined informal learning moment: a young adult Dongria woman sitting with two school-age children, helping one child draw a leaf in a notebook resting on the child's knees. Other child sits to the side and watches the drawing from a plausible angle. Children wear ordinary contemporary cotton T-shirt and trousers or simple dress, no uniform or ceremonial ornaments. Woman wears an off-white cotton wrap with narrow red border, modest necklace, short dark hair with metal clips: informed ONLY by centre/right women in attached market reference, not the tourist left, not their identities. Everyday house doorstep with green hill glimpsed beyond, no architectural claim. Focus on the pencil hand and shared notebook; believable gaze, wrists and page orientation. No writing or invented letters, no alphabet, logos, blackboard, invented school/programme, performance regalia or generic tribal decoration. Quiet natural interaction and unequal spacing. Distinct imagined people, not portraits; clear painterly illustration with selective detail and soft daylight.

images.name: 10-kuvi-and-jatapu-script
images.prompt: Wide 3:2 editorial watercolor and gouache on warm ivory paper for a careful article on Kuvi spoken language and the devised Jatapu script. An imagined quiet conversation in Niyamgiri: older Dongria woman seen in profile speaking naturally, opposite a younger adult man in an ordinary muted blue cotton shirt listening. Close waist-up scene, woman left and man right with asymmetric relaxed poses. Woman's cream drape with narrow red-pink edge, simple beads, short dark hair held with small metal pins and restrained nose/ear ornaments should follow only the two women centre/right in attached market clothing reference; not the tourist left and do not copy anyone's identity. A small open blank notebook lies between them on a plain low ledge, no pen actively writing, no recorder needed. Soft green hills partially glimpsed behind. The focal point is the conversation and attentive gaze; ordinary human warmth without exaggerated gestures. No lettering, alphabets, pseudo-script, sound waves, speech bubbles, sacred icons, performance jewellery or teaching claims. Not a named language consultant, recorded interview, classroom or documented event. Distinct imagined faces and selective painterly detail, physically believable hands and clothing.
